newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court denies NYNEX dismissal motion.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court denies NYNEX dismissal motion.

text.p: A New York State appeals court has ruled that a class action suit may proceed against NYNEX Corp over its failure to protect the confidentiality of customers who asked to have their phone numbers shielded from the company's caller identification service, plaintiffs attorneys said Wednesday.
The decision, issued July 3, means that the case may now proceed to trial in New York Supreme Court in Albany County, said attorney G. Oliver Koppell of the firm Meyer, Suozzi, English & Klein PC.
Koppell said the case has three named plaintiffs but may involve up to 40,000 people whose phone numbers were revealed against their wishes through NYNEX's "Caller I.D." service.

Koppell said NYNEX admitted to the computer error about two years ago when complaints were initially filed with the New York Public Service Commission. NYNEX conceded it had allowed at least 30,000 customers' phone numbers to be revealed through Caller ID despite requests from those customers that their numbers be blocked out, Koppell said.
The Public Service Commission ordered the problem corrected and NYNEX has done so.
The incident occurred over a period of about two-and-a-half years, from mid-1992 until the end of 1994, Koppell said.
NYNEX spokesman John Bonomo said the company could not comment on pending litigation.

The appellate court ruled on an appeal filed by NYNEX over a state Supreme Court judge's determinations in September and December 1996 to allow the case to proceed and to grant class action certification to the plaintiffs.

The court rejected NYNEX arguments that it was protected from such action because the public service commission previously had take action on the matter, Koppell said. The court also rejected the Baby Bell company's contention that it was protected by a disclaimer included in the tariff filed with the commission.
The case may be ready for trial within a year, he said.
